ios.desc:
PeekCard lets you scan and store barcodes and QR codes for loyalty cards, gym passes, tickets, and more. With widgets, you can access your cards instantly.

No more digging through your wallet or carrying around stacks of plastic. With PeekCard you can:

- Scan any barcode: QR codes, EAN, Code 128, and more.
- Organize your cards with names and colors for easy access.
- Open them instantly with widgets.
- Travel light without leaving your cards behind.
- Perfect for rewards programs, event tickets, memberships, and everyday essentials.

quotes.text:
A little over a year ago I created a little app to store QR or barcodes and use them either from the app or through a widget, it's called PeekCard [1].

I was wondering if iOS 27 Wallet opening up custom passes was going to mean I could abandon my little app, but for me it's not the right solution. It creates large portrait size passes which are designed to contain meta info about the cards purpose. What I want is a name, color and the QR or barcode. With the "Create a Pass" in Wallet I get these big things, almost all space wasted with a relatively small barcode that I can't use as a widget. So for me it's a "no", I'll stick with my own app.

[1] https://apps.apple.com/app/peekcard/id6749822787

Some time ago I built a really simple app to do this as well, called PeekCard[1]. But I actually hope Apple Wallet does it better. What I'm wondering about is whether there will be decent barcode support and if it will support widgets.

[1]: https://apps.apple.com/app/peekcard/id6749822787
quotes.story_title: iOS 27 is adding a 'Create a Pass' button to Apple Wallet
